dialogue.speaker: Samer

dialogue.speaker: Lina

dialogue.speaker: Samer

lessons.culture: In Lebanon people say دقّ (da22) for ringing someone, so دقيلي means call me, and a call usually opens with ألو followed by مين معي؟ to find out who is on the line. Ending with يسلمو or مع السلامة rather than hanging up abruptly is the polite habit.

exercises.prompt: You pick up the phone and don't know who is calling. Answer naturally, asking who it is.

too_formal.feedback: Correct Arabic, but much more formal than how people answer the phone in Lebanon.

exercises.tip: ألو then مين معي؟ is the everyday opening.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you on the phone: شو الأخبار؟ Say all is good, thank God.

too_formal.item: الأمور على ما يرام، ولله الحمد

exercises.tip: الحمد لله almost always turns up in the answer.

exercises.prompt: Complete: ما قدرت _____ عليك من شوي. Meaning: I couldn't answer you a bit ago.

exercises.tip: فيك is the everyday can you in Lebanese.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but with a written case ending nobody says on the phone.

exercises.tip: مشغول means busy, for a line or a person.

lessons.culture: In Beirut a meeting place is usually named by a landmark or a well-known cafe, such as the Raouche rocks or a cafe on Hamra Street, since street addresses are rarely used in daily talk. Arriving ten or fifteen minutes late is common, which is why إذا تأخرت دقلي is a routine thing to say.

lessons.culture: Plans shift often in Lebanon because of traffic and work, and asking to postpone is not rude if you add معليش and a short reason. The other person usually answers ولا يهمك, and a new day is often offered with إن شاء الله.

challenge.title: A Phone Call to Rearrange Plans
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a phone conversation of at least 10 lines. It must include answering the phone, proposing a place and a time to meet, changing that plan for a real reason, agreeing on a new time or place, and, if the person you called is not free, leaving a message for someone else to pass on.
required_elements: Asking or stating who is calling, using مين معي or معك + name.
A suggestion of where to meet, using خلينا نتلاقى or a similar phrase.
A question about time, using أي ساعة بتناسبك.
A reason for changing the plan, using طلعتلي شغلة or a similar phrase.
A request to postpone or change, using فينا نأجل or بدي غيّر الموعد.
An apology for the change, using آسف or معليش.
A reassurance in response, using ولا يهمك.
At least one exchange about leaving or taking a message, using رسالة or قلّو.
